messages:
Jordan (Support): Hey team — customer AcmeAI reporting a sudden spike and a bunch of 429s around 11:03 UTC. They say they had a short burst of traffic for ~45s and then client started getting errors. Attaching sample response header they pasted from logs:

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 11:03:12 GMT
x-rw-rate-limit: 1000
x-rw-rate-remaining: 0
x-rw-burst-credits: 0
retry-after: 10

Jordan (Support): They said they were doing ~120 rps for 30s, avg token length ~600 tokens. Plan: hosted PAYG. Any immediate mitigation?

Sam L (Support Eng): Thanks — can you DM the customer_id and the exact timestamps? Also want their SDK version. Short term: advise exponential backoff + jitter to clients. Long-term we might bump burst credits per account if it's legitimate traffic.

Priya G (SRE): Copying what we know: our burst system is a token-bucket style credit that refills at config rate and allows short spikes. If x-rw-burst-credits hits 0 the router returns 429s until bucket refills. Default smoothing window is 60s (we smooth token emission across 60s). At 120 rps with 600 tokens/request that can chew credits fast.

Kim (Eng-Platform): @Jordan @Sam quick note — there are two knobs: server-side burst bucket (per-customer) and smoothing policy used by the gateway (how aggressively we smooth across seconds). We typically avoid increasing permanent burst for PAYG without a guard. We can temporarily increase the bucket for this customer for 10 minutes and monitor.

burst-bot: auto-notice: customer_id=acct_01GHTZ — burst_credits_consumed=980 in last 45s; bucket_now=0

Ethan (SRE): For immediate customer advice: 1) implement client-side smoothing (throttle to sustainable rps), 2) reduce requested tokens per call if possible, 3) implement retry with full jitter using Retry-After header. Example JS backoff pattern we give customers:
```js
// naive smoothing + backoff
const queue = [];
let inflight = 0;
const MAX_CONCURRENCY = 8; // tune
function sendNext() {
  if (!queue.length || inflight >= MAX_CONCURRENCY) return;
  inflight++;
  const req = queue.shift();
  fetch(req.url, req.opts).then(res => {
    if (res.status === 429) {
      const ra = parseInt(res.headers.get('retry-after') || '1', 10);
      // requeue with jitter
      setTimeout(() => queue.push(req), ra * 1000 + Math.random() * 500);
    }
  }).finally(() => { inflight--; sendNext(); });
}
setInterval(sendNext, 100); // keep draining
```
Jordan (Support): Customer wants a clear one-paragraph explainer I can send them. Also they asked if this is a billing-related throttle or safety throttle.

Sam L (Support Eng): Short explainer to send: "You hit a short, high-volume burst that exhausted your account's temporary burst credits. Burst credits let short spikes go through but can be exhausted if requests are large or sustained. We recommend adding client-side smoothing and using retries with jitter. We can temporarily increase your burst allowance while we review traffic patterns."

Priya G (SRE): To add technical detail for the team: when the gateway sees a request it checks the token-bucket. If credits available, it deducts cost = tokens_requested * cost_per_token. For embeddings/large responses large token counts mean each request consumes more credits. Smoothing policy tries to spread consumption across window W (60s default) — if requests cluster within W you still hit 0. We also expose x-rw-burst-credits header so clients can observe remaining credits.

Kim (Eng-Platform): Action proposal: 1) temporary +5k burst credits to acct_01GHTZ for 10m (manual override), 2) enable short canary of smoothing window change (reduce window to 30s for this customer to allow faster refill) — note reducing window changes refill behavior so test carefully, 3) recommend client smoothing sample to customer. Thoughts?

Ethan (SRE): I would NOT reduce window to 30s for PAYG — that increases allowed short bursts unexpectedly. If the goal is to let them recover faster, we should increase bucket size temporarily. Window reduction is messy.

Kim (Eng-Platform): Good point @Ethan. Let's do temp bucket bump. We have a playbook for temporary burst increases in the console. I'll file the change and keep it on a 10-minute timer.

Jordan (Support): Customer provided repro script and times — posting snippet they used (calls parallel 200 sockets):
```bash
for i in {1..600}; do
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"prompt":"...","max_tokens":600}' &
done
wait
```
Jordan (Support): Also included their SDK logs showing lots of 429s and consistent Retry-After of 10s.

burst-bot: notice: manual_override_grant started by Kim (Eng-Platform) -> +5000 burst credits for acct_01GHTZ; expires in 10m

Sam L (Support Eng): I'm composing customer message now. Also adding mitigation steps for them: a) use queueing to limit concurrent requests b) batch prompts when possible to reduce per-request overhead c) respect retry-after header and add jitter.

Priya G (SRE): Post-mortem notes for internal: we should add a runbook section on how large-token requests interact with burst accounting; add an example calc: 120 rps * 600 tokens * cost = X credits/min. Also let's add telemetry to alert when a single account consumes >50% of burst pool in <60s.

Jordan (Support): Customer notified: we increased burst credits for 10m and recommended client-side smoothing. They replied "thanks, tests look better now" and error rate dropped after 90s.

Kim (Eng-Platform): I'll follow up with a narrow console UI change to make temporary burst grants easier and track them on the billing side. Filing internal ticket ENG-PLAT-742 for that.

Ethan (SRE): Recommend we ship a small doc in support playbooks: "How to diagnose 429s: check x-rw-burst-credits, x-rw-rate-remaining, token size, and concurrent sockets" — I'll draft this.

Sam L (Support Eng): Customer-facing follow-up sent and scheduled a brief sync with AcmeAI for tomorrow to discuss traffic shaping.

Jordan (Support): Marking thread resolved for now. :white_check_mark: if problems return reopen and we'll escalate to infra oncall.

Kim (Eng-Platform): Thanks everyone. Filing follow-ups: ENG-PLAT-742 (console temp-burst UI), SRE-333 (alert on rapid burst consumption), DOCS-119 (customer-facing guidance).

Jordan (Support): Closing thread.
